summary: Chiko Corona works in Buddhist studies and studied under traditional teachers Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Koyasan University, where he was attested as professor in 1970 and as part-time lecturer in 1980.

Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar around 1955–1958 and held a post at the British Library around 1970–1985.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, studying under Thomé H. Fang, Bingnan Li, and Lobsang Palden Tenpe Dronme. He held posts at Chinese Culture University, Griffith University, and Pure Land Learning College Association.

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Harvard University (~2001–2009) and studied at UT Austin. Around 2011, he served as Associate Professor at National Chengchi University.

Ching-mei Shyu works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Jan Nattier and completed a PhD at Cornell University by 2008 under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Chintaharan Chakravarti (1900–1972) was an Indology scholar who served as Professor at Presidency University, held a post at Bethune College (attested 1941), and was Publication Secretary at Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat (attested 1960).

Chintaman Ganesh Kashikar (1910–2007) worked in Indology. He served as Assistant Secretary at Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala (attested 1941) and as Professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) specializes in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University, serving as its Director in 1996.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He held posts at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Sōji-ji, and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968), served as assistant professor at Hanazono University (~1978–1985), and was a professor at Tokoha University (attested 1989).

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Kōkōdō. He served as a professor at Otani University (1919) and founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She earned a doctorate from the University of Vienna (1990–1994) and served as lecturer, associate professor, and professor (2011) at the University of Tsukuba.
Chlodwig H. Werba (born 1947) is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, attested between 1990 and 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Kunga Chophel, Geshe Tsechok, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and was Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery in 1928.
Chogyū Takayama (1871–1902) worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School (~1886–1891) and the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896).
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (1829–1870) was an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and trained under traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).
Chris Clark works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon by 2015 and served as an honorary associate there (attested 2019).
